comparator.name: Biology
comparator.sourceNotes: The current official programme pages establish a coherent 180-EC Biology pathway. Year 1 contains 60 EC of broad compulsory biology, medical-biology, mathematics, statistics and research preparation. Year 2 contains 36 EC of compulsory study and 24 EC of domain-specialisation/elective space. Year 3 contains a 3-EC Biology Essay, 3 EC of Personal and Professional Development, 42 EC of domain-specialisation/elective space and a 12-EC research-department internship. The zero-credit introductory programme and Research Skills requirement remain compulsory but fall outside the 180-EC credit-bearing component list. The generic target offers seven named domain specialisations plus an eighth Free domain for students who do not want to select one domain; that least-specialised official option is selected independently of UCR fit, and its genuine profiling space is preserved rather than filled with invented courses.

alternatives.label: Biology across organisms, ecosystems & health
alternatives.concept: A broad closest feasible biology programme spanning biodiversity, evolution, ecosystems and environmental systems alongside molecular and cellular biology, biochemistry, physiology, neuroscience, genetics, disease and laboratory, statistical and computational methods.
alternatives.labelReason: The curriculum gives substantial weight to organismal and ecological biology and to human health and molecular biology, so the label describes its broad biological span rather than presenting one subfield as dominant.
progression: Life-science, sustainability and biodiversity foundations precede molecular cell biology, laboratory work, ecology, physiology, biochemistry, advanced genetics, disease, pharmacology, environmental science and sustainability governance. All formal prerequisites occur earlier and every course is offered in its assigned term.

alternatives.label: Ecology, climate & environmental biology
alternatives.concept: An ecological and environmental-biology route organised around organisms, biodiversity, ecosystems and evolution under climate and environmental change, with conservation, Earth-system science, field and spatial methods, sustainability and environmental governance.
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum is dominated by ecology, biodiversity, environmental science, climate, conservation and sustainability, with methods and governance supporting that biological focus.
alternatives.distinctness: Compared with the broad closest match, this route replaces twelve courses in molecular, biomedical, physiological and disease study with climate, conservation, environmental systems, spatial observation, soils, adaptation, sustainable farming and environmental-justice study.
progression: Sustainability, biodiversity, climate and ecosystem foundations precede evolution, conservation, environmental analysis, marine biology, biogeochemistry, spatial methods and advanced sustainability research. Sustainability Essentials I precedes Sustainability Essentials II, Earth Observation, Earth System Science Tools and Earth's Resources. All formal prerequisites occur earlier and every course is offered in its assigned term.

alternatives.label: Human biology, disease & neuroscience
alternatives.concept: A medical-biology route connecting cells, molecules, genetics, physiology, infection and disease with brain biology, cognition, development, diagnosis, treatment and laboratory, statistical and population research.
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum has a clear human and medical-biology centre, integrating molecular disease mechanisms and physiology with neuroscience, cognition, health psychology and biomedical research.
alternatives.distinctness: Compared with the closest programme, this route replaces ten ecology, evolution, sustainability, conservation and environmental courses with a sequenced brain-and-behaviour, cognition, health psychology, development, diagnosis and research strand; it differs from the environmental route by twenty-two courses.
progression: Life, health, biomedicine, brain and behaviour foundations precede molecular cell biology, laboratory work, physiology, biochemistry, neurobiology, cognition, disease, pharmacology, diagnostics and advanced research. Foundation of Life, Health & Biomedicine and Introduction to Brain & Behavior precede every course that formally requires them, and every course is offered in its assigned term.

candidates.label: Microbiology, functional genomics and physiological adaptation

routeSelection.basis: The normalized target is the generic Biology bachelor. The official curriculum offers seven subject-specific domain specialisations and an eighth Free domain explicitly intended for students who cannot or do not want to select one domain. The Free domain is therefore the least specialised official continuation of the broad first-year foundation and is selected independently of UCR fit.

selection.assessment: The closest programme preserves the broad span from organisms and ecosystems to molecules, human physiology, neuroscience and disease. The ecology/environment cluster and the human-biology/neurobiology cluster each support a coherent additional route. A separate microbiology, functional-genomics and physiological-adaptation candidate remains academically valid but cannot be added after the three-programme maximum is reached. The included pairs differ by twelve, ten and twenty-two courses respectively, so every pair exceeds the 30-EC distinctness floor. The maximum of three alternatives is reached.

notes.text: Both programmes cover substantial organismal, ecological, molecular, human and research biology. Radboud additionally requires dedicated work in plant evolution and physiology, microbiology and microbial metabolism, histology, two statistics courses, mathematics for biologists, scientific writing, extensive domain-specialisation space and a research-department internship. UCR can build broad, environmental and human-biological programmes, but it does not reproduce every specialist laboratory and organismal sequence.
